Edition No. 3Covering September 28–October 5, 2026Published October 5, 2026

Toyota Closes In, Detroit Slips and a 90-Minute Sellout

Third-quarter sales put Detroit's share of the market at a record low as Toyota's hybrids closed to within 38,000 vehicles of GM. The new fuel-economy rule went to court, the EV market split a year after the tax credit, and Ram sold a year of V8 Rumble Bees in an hour and a half.

By Margot Devries · 19 minute read

In this edition

  1. Detroit's share hits a record low as Toyota's hybrids close in on GM
  2. The new fuel-economy rule goes to court
  3. One year after the tax credit, the EV market splits
  4. A year of V8 Rumble Bees, gone in 90 minutes
  5. Volkswagen trades the ID.4 name for an electric Tiguan
  6. Hyundai will build the Tucson Hybrid in Alabama
  7. What if the road became the charger?

The week's theme was the hybrid dividend. With gasoline at a record for September and the average new vehicle above $50,000, buyers moved toward thriftier cars, and the companies that sell hybrids in volume took the share. Detroit's fell to a record low while Toyota's electrified share passed 57%. The rule that sets America's long-term fuel-economy target went to court. EVs fell back a year after the tax credit, except where the product fit the buyer, like Rivian's R2 and Europe's smaller, cheaper models. Then Ram sold a year of V8 muscle trucks in 90 minutes, and Honda unveiled technology for a road that charges trucks as they drive. As always, every story carries a status line, because a final count, a forecast and a promise in a press release are not the same kind of news.

Markets · United States

Confirmed sales figures · the record-low share is Cox Automotive's forecast · Toyota model figures are Carveyance calculations

Detroit's Share Hits a Record Low as Toyota's Hybrids Close In on GM

GM kept the US sales crown for the third quarter by only 37,751 vehicles. More than half of everything Toyota sold was electrified, and the Detroit 3 sold barely more than a third of America's new vehicles.

DETROIT — Third-quarter sales reports, released October 1 and 2, bore out what Cox Automotive forecast a week earlier: GM, Ford and Stellantis together took "just over 36%" of the US market from July through September, which Cox calls the lowest share on record. Asian automakers took more than half for the second quarter in a row.

GM is still No. 1, but its sales fell 5.5% while Toyota and Lexus edged up 0.6%. Ford, down 6.6%, also lost about a week of F-150 production at 2 plants in late September to a supplier shortage. Hyundai Motor Group, which outsold Ford in July and August, set a third-quarter record, with Hyundai and Kia each posting their best third quarter ever. Honda had its best third quarter since 2019. At Stellantis, Ram rose 29% and Jeep fell 20%, leaving the group flat.

Toyota's hybrid lineup did the work

Toyota said 57.4% of its third-quarter US sales, Toyota and Lexus together, were electrified: 363,367 vehicles, up 28.5%, nearly all of them hybrids. The RAV4 and Camry, 2 of its best-sellers, now come only as hybrids, and hybrid versions run through most of the rest of the lineup. The rivals with hybrids grew too: Honda had its best hybrid quarter ever, at more than 106,000, and Hyundai Motor Group's hybrids rose 53.4% to 138,112.

Toyota's hybrids grew. The Prius didn't.

The one Toyota hybrid going backward is the one that started it all. Regular Prius hybrid sales are down 51% this year, to 16,731 through September; in September alone Toyota sold 25,350 Camry hybrids. Buyers want hybrid fuel economy in the body style they already wanted, and Toyota now offers it nearly everywhere.

Why the gap is closing

Hybrids are one reason. Fuel and price are the others. Regular gasoline averaged a record $4.33 a gallon in September, according to AAA, 50 cents above the previous September record, and diesel set its own record, $6.53, on September 22. The average new vehicle cost $50,090 in August, Cox says, and J.D. Power estimated the average monthly payment reached $821 in September, a record for the month. Detroit's strength is full-size pickups and big SUVs, the most profitable vehicles in the market, and they are still selling. They are simply a smaller share of a market moving toward cheaper, thriftier cars.

The Carveyance take

Market share isn't profit, and Detroit still owns the full-size pickup. The bigger shift is that a hybrid is no longer a car you seek out. At Toyota it's simply how most of the lineup comes, and that's what Detroit is now selling against.

What to watch: fourth-quarter results in early January, whether Hyundai Motor Group passes Ford for a full quarter, and how close Toyota finishes the year to GM.

Policy · United States

Petition filed October 2 · no ruling yet · the rule remains in effect

The New Fuel-Economy Rule Goes to Court

20 states, Washington, D.C., and 4 cities asked a federal appeals court to review the 34.9 mpg target, in the same week gasoline closed out a record September.

BOSTON — A coalition of 20 states, including California, Colorado, Michigan and New York, plus the District of Columbia and 4 cities, filed a petition on October 2 asking the US Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to review the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration's new fuel-economy rule. The rule, finalized September 28, sets a fleet average of 34.9 mpg for model year 2031, against roughly 50.4 mpg under the 2024 rule, and ends credit trading between automakers from model year 2028.

The petition argues the rule breaks the federal requirement that standards be set at the "maximum feasible" level. The 2 sides count the money differently. The Transportation Department estimates the rule takes about $1,300 off the price of an average new vehicle; the states say drivers lose nearly $220 billion in fuel savings over time. A ruling is likely months away, and the rule stays in force unless the court pauses it.

What the pump says

The case lands while fuel is expensive. Regular averaged $4.33 a gallon in September, a record for the month, and was still $4.41 on October 1, $1.25 above a year earlier. Diesel set records too. The Energy Information Administration's weekly average peaked at $6.529 on September 21 before easing to $6.382 a week later.

Neither the rule nor the lawsuit changes what's on dealer lots this year. A fleet average isn't a per-car number, and Congress cut the penalty for missing a CAFE target to $0 in 2025.

The Carveyance take

For buyers, the near-term effect is close to zero either way. What the case changes is planning. Automakers deciding which engines to keep past 2028 now have a rule whose future depends on a court.

What to watch: the court's schedule, whether any automaker or trade group joins the case, and the EIA's weekly fuel update every Monday.

Electric vehicles · United States and Europe

Confirmed company figures · Tesla's are global · European totals come from Transport & Environment, an advocacy group

One Year After the Tax Credit, the EV Market Splits

GM's EV sales fell by more than 60% against last year's rush to beat the credit. Rivian had the best quarter in its history on the cheaper R2, and in Europe, Stellantis can't get enough batteries.

DETROIT — The comparison is unkind by design. In the third quarter of 2025, buyers raced to claim the $7,500 federal EV tax credit before it expired on September 30. A year later, without it, GM sold 25,473 EVs in the US, down 61.7%. The Chevrolet Equinox EV, GM's best-selling EV a year ago, fell 92.4% to 1,905. Cadillac's 4 EVs made up nearly half of GM's total, at 12,358. Hyundai Motor Group's EV sales fell 51%, to 22,311.

Tesla, which doesn't report US sales separately, delivered 486,532 vehicles worldwide, down 2.1% from its record third quarter of 2025 but about 5% more than Wall Street expected. It built 464,391, so it sold more cars than it made. The cleaner test comes next quarter: the fourth quarter of 2025 was the first without the credit, so this year's fourth quarter will be the first like-for-like comparison.

Where EVs are growing

Rivian delivered 19,248 vehicles, the most in its history, as the smaller, cheaper R2 SUV, which began reaching customers in the second quarter, came off the line in volume. It built 19,751 and kept its forecast of 65,000 to 70,000 deliveries for the year. The wider US market fell; the right product still grew.

Europe is the counterargument. EV sales in the EU reached a record 1.64 million from January through August, up 45%, for 22% of the market, according to Transport & Environment, which credits a wave of smaller, cheaper models launched to meet EU emissions targets. Some versions are selling faster than they can be built. Stellantis said it will pause its Sochaux and Rennes plants in France in late October because its battery joint venture, ACC, can't supply enough long-range packs for the electric Peugeot 3008 and 5008 and the Citroën C5 Aircross. Stellantis says demand for those versions, especially from fleets, exceeds what it can supply.

The Carveyance take

The EV market isn't one story anymore. In America, the end of the credit showed which EVs people buy without a subsidy, and the R2 is one of them. In Europe, size and price are driving growth. The EVs that work are the ones built for the buyer, not for the incentive.

What to watch: Tesla's earnings on October 21, Rivian's on October 29, and the fourth quarter as the first like-for-like test without the credit.

Trucks · United States

Confirmed by Stellantis · disclosed October 1 · allocation size not given

A Year of V8 Rumble Bees, Gone in 90 Minutes

Ram's 395-hp short-bed muscle truck starts at $62,790 with destination. Its allocation for the rest of 2026 sold out in an hour and a half.

AUBURN HILLS, Mich. — Stellantis put it in a single line of its third-quarter sales release on October 1: orders opened for the 5.7-liter 2027 Ram 1500 Rumble Bee, and the initial allocation for the 2026 calendar year sold out in 90 minutes. Ram hasn't said how many trucks that was.

The Rumble Bee is a Quad Cab with a short bed, widened fenders, a wheelbase shortened by 13 inches and full-time four-wheel drive. The 5.7-liter Hemi V8 version makes 395 hp and starts at $59,995 before $2,795 destination, and reaches dealers this quarter. A 470-hp 6.4-liter Rumble Bee 392 and a 777-hp supercharged Rumble Bee SRT at $94,995 follow in the first half of 2027.

Ram's sales rose 29% in the quarter to 134,072, and Ram 1500 sales jumped 73% to 76,650. The Hemi V8 came back to the Ram 1500 for 2026, a year after Ram dropped it.

The Carveyance take

"Sold out" describes an allocation, not a year of production. Still, demand for a $60,000 short-bed pickup with a V8 was strong enough to clear Ram's first batch in an hour and a half. With the federal fuel-economy penalty at $0, a V8 truck costs its maker nothing extra in fines, and Ram is betting there are plenty of buyers who want one.

What to watch: how many trucks the 2026 allocation was, confirmed pricing for the 392, and first deliveries before year's end.

Electric vehicles · Germany

Announced · full reveal due in October · on sale in Europe in early 2027 · US timing not given

Volkswagen Trades the ID.4 Name for an Electric Tiguan

The ID. Tiguan will replace both the ID.4 and the ID.5 and sit beside the gasoline and hybrid Tiguans. Volkswagen is betting buyers trust a name they already know.

WOLFSBURG, Germany — Volkswagen said on September 28 that its next electric compact SUV will be called the ID. Tiguan and will replace both the ID.4 and the coupe-styled ID.5. It will be sold alongside the gasoline and hybrid Tiguans. The full reveal is due in October and European sales begin in early 2027. Volkswagen has confirmed a North American version but hasn't said when, and it hasn't published battery, range, charging or pricing details.

The ID.4 and ID.5 have sold more than 950,000 units since 2021. The Tiguan name carries more: Volkswagen says it has built more than 8.3 million of them. The company has already made the same move at the small end of its range with the ID. Polo.

The Carveyance take

Separate EV names were meant to announce a new beginning. A familiar name tells a buyer something more useful: the electric version is the same car with a different powertrain. Expect more automakers to do the same.

What to watch: the full reveal this month, range and pricing, and where the North American version will be built.

Manufacturing · Alabama

Announced investment · no start date for the Tucson Hybrid · Santa Fe EREV due in the first half of 2027

Hyundai Will Build the Tucson Hybrid in Alabama

A $500 million investment brings production home from Korea, adds an extended-range Santa Fe in 2027, and comes with a pickup planned for 2030.

DETROIT — Hyundai Motor's chief executive, José Muñoz, announced a $500 million investment in Hyundai's Montgomery, Alabama, plant on September 30 at the Automotive News Congress. Every Tucson Hybrid sold in the US is now imported from Ulsan, South Korea. The money moves its production to Alabama and pays for next-generation engines, hybrid components and powertrains for extended-range electric vehicles, or EREVs: electric cars that carry a gasoline engine as a generator. The first, a Santa Fe EREV, is due in the first half of 2027. Hyundai didn't give a start date for the Tucson Hybrid.

Hyundai also said it is developing a body-on-frame pickup for 2030, in the segment GM, Ford and Stellantis dominate. Hyundai Motor Group sold 138,112 hybrids in the third quarter, up 53.4%. A vehicle imported from South Korea pays a 15% US tariff; one built in Alabama doesn't.

The Carveyance take

Hybrid demand is now steady enough to justify an American assembly line. Muñoz said in April that about half of Hyundai's US sales are built here. Moving the Tucson Hybrid raises that share and takes a tariff out of its cost.

What to watch: a start date for Alabama-built Tucson Hybrids, Santa Fe EREV pricing, and where the pickup will be built.

Technology · Japan

Technology developed · public-road test from April 2027 · no cost or commercial plan yet

What If the Road Became the Charger?

Honda has built units that sit under the pavement and charge an electric truck as it drives over them. A test on a Japanese expressway starts in 2027.

TOKYO — Honda said on October 5 that it has developed the core technology to charge electric vehicles wirelessly while they move, including heavy trucks. Units buried in the road send power by magnetic coupling to a receiver under the vehicle, the same principle as a wireless phone charger on a far larger scale. Honda R&D built the road and vehicle units. The construction companies Taisei and Taisei Rotec built the DC power supply and the methods for setting it into pavement.

Testing at a private facility starts late this year and includes a durability run of 1 million wheel passes. A public-road trial on the Tateyama Expressway in Chiba follows from Japan's 2027 fiscal year, which begins in April 2027. Honda is aiming at trucks of about 20,000 kg (44,000 lb) and plans to verify power of up to 150 kW. It still has to prove performance at highway speed, control of stray magnetic fields and long-term reliability, and it hasn't said what the system would cost to install.

Why a charging road matters

A truck that charges as it drives needs to stop less often, can carry a smaller and lighter battery, and draws its power along the highway instead of all at once at a truck stop. Honda says in-motion charging would cut how often EVs have to stop to charge, at home or at a station.

The idea has American roots. In November 2023, Michigan's Transportation Department opened a quarter-mile stretch of 14th Street in Detroit that charges equipped vehicles as they drive, built by the Israeli company Electreon. And in August 1997, researchers buried 92,778 magnets under 7.6 miles of an I-15 carpool lane in San Diego so that 8 modified Buick LeSabres could steer themselves by sensing them. Magnets in the road have already steered cars. Honda wants the road to power them too.

The Carveyance take

Charging lanes don't need to cover every road. A few busy freight corridors, wired once, could let electric trucks run all day on smaller batteries. The open question is who pays: a bigger battery is bought by the truck's owner, a charging road by whoever builds the highway.

What to watch: Honda's demonstration at Japan Mobility Show Bizweek, October 13 to 16, and the Tateyama Expressway trial from April 2027.

Also That Week

4 more stories worth knowing, in brief.

Labor · Germany

Confirmed notice · takes effect December 31 · talks resume in mid-October

Volkswagen Gives Notice on 10 Labor Agreements

WOLFSBURG, Germany — Volkswagen gave notice on September 30 that it will end 10 in-house collective agreements in Germany on December 31, including the one that sets the 35-hour week and overtime rules, according to IG Metall and the German trade site electrive.net. The union wants 5% more pay, which Volkswagen has rejected. Warning strikes become possible from January 1, when the contract's no-strike period ends. The December 2024 agreement ruling out layoffs for operational reasons through 2030 still stands.

Why it matters: it's the second German automaker in 2 weeks to push on labor costs at home, after Mercedes put 2 plants on notice.

Launches · Texas

Postponed · new date October 15

Tesla Puts Off the Roadster Reveal

WACO, Texas — Tesla postponed its outdoor reveal of the second-generation Roadster, set for October 1, citing a forecast of severe weather, and moved it to October 15 at the same site, according to electrive. The car was first shown in November 2017 and was originally promised for 2020.

Why it matters: the Roadster is Tesla's halo car, and its final specs and price are still unknown, 9 years after it was first shown.

Recalls · United States

Recall filed · free dealer repair

Ford Recalls 41,748 Super Duty Pickups and Expeditions

DEARBORN, Mich. — Ford recalled 41,748 2026 Super Duty pickups, F-250 through F-550, and 2025 to 2027 Expedition SUVs on September 30 because contaminated LED chips can make the headlights, daytime running lights and parking lights fail without warning. Dealers will inspect the headlights and replace faulty ones free. Ford said it knew of 6 warranty claims and field reports and no crashes or injuries.

Why it matters: it covers Ford's heavy-duty pickups and its biggest SUV, and the fix is a dealer replacement, not a bulb swap in the driveway.

Retail · United States

In effect October 1 · applies to advertised prices only

Stellantis Sets a Floor on Advertised Prices

AUBURN HILLS, Mich. — From October 1, Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep and Ram dealers may not advertise vehicles below a minimum price that Stellantis sets, CBT News reported. Dealers can still sell for less; the rule covers advertising only. Stellantis said its discounting had run at more than 3 times the industry average.

Why it matters: ads for Stellantis vehicles may show higher prices, but the price at the dealer's desk is still negotiable.

Since That Week

Where last week's stories went next.

Follow-up · Tesla's driver assistance in Europe

Croatia approved Tesla's FSD (Supervised) on September 29, the latest European country to do so. The same day, the European Transport Safety Council, a road-safety advocacy group, urged EU authorities to reject 2 of its functions: a speed offset that can let the car drive as much as 50% above the limit it detects, and a setting that matches the speed of surrounding traffic. Tesla didn't immediately comment. The EU-wide vote isn't expected before December.

Follow-up · Ford's F-150 stoppage

Ford had F-150 production running again at Dearborn Truck and Kansas City Assembly by the end of September, after about a week down. It still hasn't named the supplier. Chief executive Jim Farley said the disruption cut into Ford's third-quarter wholesale truck deliveries.

Follow-up · The Chinese-car bill

The fast-track Senate vote on the Connected Vehicle Security Act, put off on September 24, had not taken place when this edition closed, as far as Carveyance could find.

Follow-up · Last week, in depth

All 4 of last week's in-depth pieces are live: The $1,300 Question on the new fuel-economy rule, Built Here, Banned Here on the Chinese-car bill, No Replacement for Displacement on GM's 8.3-liter Duramax, and Gas In, Electric Out on Nissan's e-Power.

Not final yet
Detroit's record-low 36%, which is Cox Automotive's forecast until full market data is in. Toyota's quarterly model figures, which are Carveyance calculations from its year-to-date tables.
